free_tier.stated: Explicit, from their own page: 'No, we have no storage or bandwidth limits. We only have a 5GB per file limit.' Help centre repeats: 'Payhip supports a maximum file size of 5GB per digital product.'
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: No bandwidth limit stated (their words: 'no storage or bandwidth limits'). Free plan is 'Free Forever' with a 5% transaction fee. No monthly fee, so an unpriced/cheap product costs ~nothing.

interface_detail: Web upload. REST API + webhooks on paid plans; the digital-product upload itself is form-based.
chaining: 5 GB/file x unlimited files per product x unlimited products = unbounded account. Every listing is a shard with its own 5 GB ceiling. The cleanest 'shard into 5 GB pieces' target found.
limits_note: Per-object-cap 5 GB. The only limit they publish. Extension blocklist is a hard gate on ingress: EXE, ISO, DMG, VBS, SCR refused unless inside a ZIP. No aggregate quota.

identity_cost.detail: a first name, last name, email address and password on the free-account form. No card is asked for: the help centre adds card details only to upgrade a paid plan. No phone field is on the form.

reliability_note: Serving path is fine; the operational risk is that a 'digital product' must be a listed product, and free products still sit behind a checkout page. Buyer link is emailed, not a stable public URL. So it is an archive/delivery tier, not a hot-link CDN.

extras.agent_focus: Print-on-demand, media and fulfilment platforms that host your uploads permanently and serve them cheaply. The question for every candidate was NOT 'can I upload' (all of them accept uploads) but: does the platform serve my ORIGINAL bytes back, unsigned, indefinitely, from a CDN I can hot-link? POD image hosts (Redbubble/Printful/Printify/Society6/Threadless/Zazzle/Etsy) all re-encode, cap at 20-300 MB and gate the write behind account setup — they are inverted (tiny ingress, no egress). The value in this niche is the DIGITAL-PRODUCT fulfilment layer and the 3D-model repositories, which are the two places where arbitrary file types survive ingest at GB scale.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
